question: Can a guitarist obtain the same GA fretboard position information and available selection action through pointer, keyboard, and screen-reader paths across render modes?
production_path: investigation: observe hypothesize test conclude reflect
hypothesis: A shared position model plus a synchronized textual list, with native selection controls only when selection exists, can preserve the same musical facts and available action across SVG, Canvas, and 3D views.
evidence: At GA commit dc2e74cbd992a298f67efb928b5b3754615e1924, ReactComponents/ga-react-components/src/components/GuitarFretboard.tsx renders SVG circles with mouse enter/leave and click handlers, but the inspected markers have no explicit accessible name, role, focus target, or keyboard activation.

At the same GA commit, ReactComponents/ga-react-components/src/components/RealisticFretboard.tsx attaches pointerdown/over/out handlers to Pixi markers, and StringedInstrumentFretboard.tsx routes positions and callbacks to SVG, Canvas, and 3D modes.

At the same GA commit, Apps/ga-client/src/components/SmartVoicingDisplay.tsx renders a voicing card without an onPositionClick callback; ReactComponents/ga-react-components/tests/fretboard.spec.ts checks rendering and console errors but does not establish keyboard or screen-reader operation.
W3C WCAG 2.2 Understanding 2.1.1 addresses keyboard operation of functionality: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/keyboard.html
W3C WCAG 2.2 Understanding 4.1.2 addresses programmatic name, role, value, and state: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/name-role-value.html
W3C WCAG 2.2 Understanding 1.1.1 addresses text alternatives for non-text content: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-content.html
The proposed shared list and equivalence across modes have not been implemented or tested in GA; browser and assistive-technology results are pending.
